clue.text: Cats' home?

parts.note: jazz musicians are known as cats, so their home is the birthplace of jazz, a city in Louisiana, not an animal shelter

explanation.surface: A question about where stray cats are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cats' home' in Britain is a shelter for stray cats; here 'cats' is old slang for jazz musicians, and the city meant is the birthplace of jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louisiana city is called the cradle of jazz, the home of the musicians nicknamed cats.

clue.text: Bill for one's trip

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of the word before it fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's travel costs being charged to an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like an invoice but is a bird's beak; 'trip' is the anagram signal on ONES, the possessive giving no letter of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's bill is its beak, the part of a face that sticks out.

clue.text: Old soldiers fight with punches, for example

parts.note: a war is a fight between nations
the Suffolk Punch is a heavy draught breed of horse, so punches are horses

explanation.surface: Veterans brawling and throwing punches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punches' suggests blows; the Suffolk Punch is an English breed of heavy farm horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans of many campaigns, people or horses, are figuratively called old warhorses.

clue.text: Touch first rocky reef, perhaps

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word rocky is used
perhaps suggests the word reef is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A boat brushing against a rocky reef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch' is the verb as in touching on a topic; 'perhaps' is a loose anagram signal, saying the reef's letters could be arranged otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch on a subject is to mention or allude to it in passing.

clue.text: English copper road-mending in South American republic

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: mending a road means its letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An English police officer doing roadworks in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, symbol CU; 'mending' rearranges ROAD into ADOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The country on the equator in South America is a republic with Quito as its capital.

clue.text: Uniquely the most worthy, like Brutus

definitions.text: Uniquely the most worthy, like Brutus

parts.words: Uniquely the most worthy, like Brutus
parts.note: Mark Antony in Julius Caesar calls Brutus the most honourable Roman of them all, singling him out above the rest

explanation.surface: Praise for Brutus as the worthiest man of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to Antony's line in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, 'This was the — Roman of them all'.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word for honourable and high-minded fits the most worthy person.

clue.text: Bear this expression of contempt

definitions.meaning: the honey-loving teddy of A. A. Milne's stories
an exclamation used to dismiss something as worthless

explanation.surface: A bear being sneered at.
explanation.definitionFit: Milne's bear shares his name with the scornful interjection, as in a dismissive sniff.

clue.text: Many stars sporting iron ring?

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: sporting suggests frolicking about, so the letters play into a new order

explanation.surface: Celebrities wearing an iron ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many stars' suggests celebrities but means a constellation; 'sporting' shuffles IRON with O, the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunter constellation is a group of many stars, including Betelgeuse and Rigel.

clue.text: One measures humidity in the merry-go-round

indicators.note: round suggests turning about, so the letters before it spin into a new order

explanation.surface: Damp conditions being checked at a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The last part of 'merry-go-round', 'round', is the anagram signal on THE MERRYGO.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument gauges how much moisture is in the air.

clue.text: Develop right place for a bat

definitions.meaning: a cricket batsman safe from being run out stands behind the line marked on the pitch, read as two words

explanation.surface: Advice on where to put a flying mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the white line near the stumps; a batter grounded behind it is in, and safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow is to expand; read as two words it places a cricket bat behind the batting line.

clue.text: Printer's decoration for the foot

parts.note: a small stroke added at the base of a printed letter's stem, as in Times typefaces

explanation.surface: A printer adorning someone's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Typefaces like Times add a small finishing stroke at the base of each letter stroke.

clue.text: Stiff, ill-shaped bun taken to final

indicators.note: something ill-shaped is badly formed, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the final part of something is its ending

explanation.surface: A stale, misshapen bun brought out at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-shaped' rearranges BUN into UNB, followed by ENDING for 'final'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rigid who will not flex or yield is stiff in manner or body.

clue.text: Stir food?

definitions.meaning: slang for prison, as in a stretch inside
oatmeal boiled in milk or water

explanation.surface: An instruction to stir the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like a cooking instruction but is slang for prison; British slang for a prison sentence is the same word as the oat breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for time in jail is also the name of the oat breakfast.

clue.text: Round number in centre of door, perhaps

indicators.note: means the number letter sits in the middle of the other piece
perhaps suggests the word door is one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A house number painted in the middle of a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DOOR into RODO, and N goes into its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical form with a recurring theme is a type of round.

clue.text: Do deeds fit constitution of Welsh assembly?

indicators.note: the constitution of something is its make-up, so the letters are made up anew

explanation.surface: A question of whether actions suit a Welsh body's rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitution of' rearranges DO DEEDS FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh festival of music and poetry is a gathering, or assembly, of bards.

clue.text: Such a trader doing time, right?

parts.note: a prisoner doing time is inside

explanation.surface: A dealer serving a prison sentence, asking whether that is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such a trader' points to the phrase for someone dealing on secret company knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trading illegally on confidential company knowledge is a dealer with privileged access.

clue.text: Gay society-girl broadcasting

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering society
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A cheerful debutante on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' here has its older sense of light-hearted and carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: In its old sense of carefree and jaunty, this matches suave, cheerful charm.

clue.text: Long walk of cruel pirates

indicators.note: cruel treatment knocks the letters of the word pirates into a new order

explanation.surface: A gruelling march imposed by heartless buccaneers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruel' rearranges PIRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiring trudge from place to place is a long walk.

clue.text: Budding Latin poet translated

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A promising Roman poet's work rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges LATIN POET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something budding is not yet realised but has the capacity to develop.

clue.text: Cricket strip where engines are tried out

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a bed is a strip of ground, as in a flower bed

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch doubling as a place to trial engines.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a top international cricket match; a garden bed is a strip of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A rig or site for trialling new machinery is the place engines are run.

clue.text: Rides so rough in collection of papers

indicators.note: rough handling knocks the letters of the words into a new order

explanation.surface: A bumpy journey while carrying a bundle of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges RIDES SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A file holding documents on one subject is a collection of papers.

clue.text: Stir herb-tea to infuse

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters of the word that follows into a new order

explanation.surface: Stirring a herbal tea to let it brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' rearranges HERBTEA; 'to' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil or impart, as in giving life or spirit to something, is to infuse.

clue.text: Tough old birds who work to provide hot water

definitions.meaning: old hens fit only for stewing

definitions.text: who work to provide hot water
definitions.meaning: domestic heaters that warm water for a house

explanation.surface: Elderly people working to heat the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly hens fit only for the pot share the name of the domestic water heaters.

clue.text: I need the end of good to turn me on

definitions.text: I need the end of good to turn me on

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, taken from good
turning the words me on around puts their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone saying they need a good ending to get excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' rearranges ME ON into EMON after D, the end of 'good'; the whole clue is spoken by an evil spirit that needs goodness destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil spirit, a devil, would want goodness brought to an end.

clue.text: Isle function, to produce tropical fruit

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
to go is to function or work, as a machine does

explanation.surface: An island's job is growing tropical fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweet yellow-fleshed stone fruit grows in hot climates.

clue.text: Barking man strikes it-not so lucky?

definitions.text: Barking man strikes it-not so lucky?

parts.words: Barking man strikes it-not so lucky?
parts.note: barking a leg means scraping it, so an unlucky man knocks the front of his lower leg

explanation.surface: A mad man striking something and having bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like mad or a dog's noise; to bark your shin is to scrape it painfully.
explanation.definitionFit: The front bone of the lower leg is what gets scraped when you bark your shin.

clue.text: Bank open?

explanation.surface: A one-word question about whether a bank is open.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep headland and a hearty, plain-spoken manner share this word.

clue.text: Deadly sin venal, troubled Albert left unknown

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the remaining letters are rearranged
left means the letters for Albert have departed from the word venal

parts.note: Al is the short form of the name Albert
in algebra Y stands for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A corrupt, troubled Albert leaves behind something deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing Albert leaves VEN, which 'troubled' then rearranges; 'left' is the verb 'departed', not the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Covetousness of others' good fortune is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Soldier, after enjoyment, throws dice — I polish off mushrooms!

indicators.note: after means the soldier comes behind the enjoyment piece

parts.note: fun means enjoyment
GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: throwing dice tumbles them, so their letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier gambling for fun and boasting of eating mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throws' rearranges DICE into CIDE; GI is an American private.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical that kills mould and fungi would boast of destroying mushrooms.

clue.text: Top knocked off foot-swelling in marriage

indicators.note: means the first letter is removed from the word for the swelling

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling at the base of the big toe

explanation.surface: A swollen foot injured during a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top knocked off' removes B from BUNION.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is the joining of two people in wedlock.

clue.text: Decline in health is work to doctor

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Ill health means a trip to the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: OP, an opus or work, is added to DR, the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall or dip in condition, such as a fall in health, is a decline.

clue.text: Naively, with heart and soul, following faith

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the faith piece

parts.note: trust and faith are synonyms
doing something heart and soul is doing it fully

explanation.surface: Devotion pursued wholeheartedly out of religious belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' is the charade signal: the 'heart and soul' piece follows the 'faith' piece rather than being part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting naively is acting with innocent, unquestioning belief in others.
